summary: OpenAI published first performance results for Jalapeño, its custom inference chip, showing higher throughput-per-watt and lower latency than comparison NVIDIA GB200/GB300 systems across GPT-OSS, DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K2.5 models, with deployment into OpenAI's own infrastructure planned by year end.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI discloses measured results for its own first-generation custom inference chip displacing merchant NVIDIA accelerators in its serving stack.
mechanisms.quote: Jalapeño is working first-party silicon with measured results, and it is the beginning of a multigenerational platform.

mechanisms.reason: The chip is stated to deliver substantially more useful work per watt and per unit hardware for the same output quality, a direct efficiency gain per token.
mechanisms.quote: Across all three, Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt at peak throughput and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency than the comparison systems.

categories.reason: The announcement is entirely about a new custom AI inference accelerator and its performance relative to merchant GPU systems.
categories.quote: Since announcing Jalapeño, OpenAI’s first custom inference chip, we have been testing the chip and the system built around it.

practices.reason: The architecture and kernel co-design techniques described (data-locality, KV-cache placement, AI-generated kernels) are stated plainly but are tied to OpenAI's own first-party silicon and not something we could apply on our stack.
practices.quote: For selected GPT‑OSS attention and mixture-of-experts blocks, AI-generated implementations ran 1.5 to 1.8 times faster than the existing human-expert-written implementations.

practices.reason: InferenceX is named as a public benchmark for measuring full-stack serving performance that an engineering team could run against its own systems.
practices.quote: we tested it on InferenceX, a public benchmark from SemiAnalysis that measures the full process of serving an AI request.

notable_reason: First disclosed measured performance results for a frontier lab's own inference silicon versus merchant GPUs is a rare, concrete data point on the custom-silicon substitution trend.
